copies.headline: Adam Still On Top, Barely Breathing Hard
copies.body: Adam leads the league at 139.4 per game and owns a 78-32 all-play, 71 percent, best in the league — nobody has scored better, and his luck sits at -0.1, so none of it was gifted. The last three weeks are softer, though: 108.9, 170.8, 106.1, an all-play of 48 percent over that stretch, and he's coming off a loss. Kenneth Walker III is questionable, which matters when Week 11 projects 123 against Kaleb. The defending champ is still Mr. Consistent. He's just mortal again.

copies.headline: 5-5 Is A Clerical Error
copies.body: Christian is 5-5 and that record is a lie. The all-play says 70-40, T-2nd of 12, and the scoring average of 127.2 ranks 3rd — he's been down 1.4 wins on what his points earned him, which is just the schedule mugging him in broad daylight. Three straight wins and a 24-9 all-play over that stretch suggests the ledger is finally balancing. Draft night graded 89, T-2nd of 12, and CeeDee Lamb, Chase Brown and Kittle still project 130 for Week 11 against John. The aura was real; the math just took ten weeks to admit it.

copies.headline: Logan Is 4-6 And It's Not His Fault
copies.body: The numbers say Logan is good and the standings say otherwise. 122.7 a game, 4th of 12. All-play 66-44, 4th of 12. Luck of -2.0, 12th of 12, meaning two wins got vaporized by scheduling. Points against of 1310.5 is the fewest-friendly mark in the league. The last three weeks he's gone 146.4, 130.4, 117.8 and gone nowhere. Jefferson and Burrow are doing their jobs; the roster projects 130, 4th of 12. Noah's next, which is exactly the opponent you don't want when the universe already hates you. The dress is not coming for Logan twice.

copies.headline: John Scores Like A Contender, Loses Like Everyone Else
copies.body: John is 5-5 with the 2nd-best scoring average in the league at 130.1 a game, which is its own kind of punishment. The all-play is 70-40, T-2nd of 12 — he's beating most of this league most weeks and has a .500 record to show for it, plus 1.4 wins below expectation. The worry isn't luck, it's the trend: 165.1, then 126.8, then 110.2, and a roster projecting 117 a week, 8th of 12. The big-brother bragging rights are intact. The margin for error is not.

copies.headline: Isaac's Roster Finally Woke Up Angry
copies.body: A 110.7 scoring average that ranks 10th of 12 is the résumé of a bad team, and for six weeks Isaac looked like one, bottoming out at 79.0 in Week 6. Then the roster remembered it exists: 112.8, 138.4, 130.3, and a 24-9 all-play over that stretch, T-1st of 12. The season all-play is still 49-61, so this is a comeback, not an alibi. Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley and a 132-a-week projection, 2nd of 12, mean the 5-5 is on Isaac, not the talent. Week 11 projects 135 against Leif. No more excuses.

copies.headline: Grant Is Exactly What He Looks Like
copies.body: Grant is 5-5, 5th of 12 in scoring at 118.3, 5th of 12 in all-play at 52 percent, and his luck sits at -0.2 wins. Four different measurements, same answer: dead median, no excuses available. The 148.5 last week is the ceiling he keeps teasing, and the 84.4 in Week 3 is the floor he keeps forgetting about. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Patrick Mahomes project 18 and 22, which is fine, because this roster projects 119 a week — one point above what he's already averaging. Nothing's changing on its own.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Roster Finally Showed Up Angry
copies.body: Three wins, 1301.5 points against — 11th-fewest allowed in the league means Mitchell has been shot at every week. He's -1.4 wins against expectation, which is the statistical version of walking into a door. But the last three weeks are the real story: 108.5, 128.6, 149.0, a 21-12 all-play run that's 4th of 12. Jahmyr Gibbs and Nico Collins both project 22 and 16, and the roster index of 67 says this thing was always better than 3-7. Grant's next. Good luck with that.

copies.headline: CJ Wins One, Still Scores Like Nobody
copies.body: CJ is 5-5 and owes about half a win to the schedule gods — plus-0.6 against expected, 4th-luckiest of 12. The all-play is the real tell: 48-62, and over the last three weeks 10-23, a 30% clip that's T-10th of 12 despite the W1 streak. He's averaging 111.5 a game, 8th in the league, with a season high of 134.7 back in Week 2 and nothing close since. Jonathan Taylor and Chuba Hubbard should carry more than this. Tyler Shough at quarterback is why they don't. Week 11 projects 121 against Peter.

copies.headline: 7-3 On Paper, 47% In Reality
copies.body: Leif is 7-3 and the all-play says 52-58. That's a 47% scorer with a +2.3 luck rating, second-luckiest in the league, and the second-fewest points against — he's been handed a schedule, not a résumé. The last three weeks tell it plainer: 64.7, 95.2, 129.4, and a 30% all-play over that stretch. Josh Allen and Christian McCaffrey are real, but Kyle Pitts projects at zero and the roster projects 104 a week, 10th of 12. Week 11 against Isaac at 103. The math is coming.

copies.headline: Best Draft On Record, Worst Roster Now
copies.body: Peter won the draft — 89 out of 100, first of twelve — and has spent ten weeks proving that August trophies don't cash. The all-play says 45-65, 41%, 10th of 12; the 5-5 record exists because luck is +0.9 wins, third-luckiest in the league. Three straight losses, 12-21 all-play in that window. The roster index is 23 and the reason is on the page: Bijan Robinson and A.J. Brown projected for zero, Bowers and Monangai questionable. Week 11 projects 86 against CJ. The career PF leader is scoring 111.1 a game.

copies.headline: Kaleb Is 6-4 And Nobody Knows Why
copies.body: Kaleb is 6-4 with a 40-70 all-play, which is 36 percent, 11th of 12. His 103.2 per game is 12th of 12. His points against are the fewest in the league. That is not a team, that is a horseshoe. Over three weeks he's gone 62.7, 76.8, 127.4 — a 6-27 all-play, 18 percent, dead last. The 86 draft grade was real, T-4th of 12; the roster now projects 96 a week, 12th of 12. Goff, Jeanty, Breece, three questionable receivers, and Adam waiting.

copies.headline: The Postseason Assassin Won't Reach The Postseason
copies.body: Noah drafted fine — 86 out of 100, T-4th in the league — and has spent ten weeks proving a draft grade is not a season. He's 3-7, averaging 106.1 a game (11th of 12), and his all-play record is 37-73, which is 34 percent and dead last. That's not variance; luck has him at -0.4 wins, about fair. The slide is real too: 143.1, then 109.4, then 91.4. James Cook III and Garrett Wilson are legitimate, and the roster still projects for roughly 100 a week. Five career playoff wins don't apply in November.

intro: Adam holds the top spot and it isn't an argument: 139.4 per game is 9.3 more than anyone else, and a 71% all-play means he's beating most of the league most weeks regardless of who's across from him. At the bottom, Noah's 31.6 edges out Kaleb by three tenths for last, which is its own kind of insult — Kaleb is 6-4 on a +2.4 luck rating and 103.2 a game, while Noah is 3-7 with better scoring and nothing to show for it. The mover worth watching is Mitchell, up from ninth to seventh at 3-7, because a 64% form number and -1.4 luck say the record is lying about him. Meanwhile Leif slid to ninth at 7-3, which happens when you're scoring 115.3, winning on a +2.3 luck cushion, and projected for 103 next week.
